decisions.reason: The polymer concrete drain housing remains a core, low-cost option with unresolved but potentially valuable integration prospects, so it is kept while further uncertainty resolves.
As the flagship designer shower drainage product aligned with the firm's strategic direction, its option value remains high and the risk of dropping it is very low.
The integrated-slope shower element fits the firm's move toward integrated, accessible systems and still holds real option value, so it is retained.
The backflow-protected basement floor drain has a dedicated niche, a specific launch, and proven drainage technology, so it remains a valuable option.
The air-admittance valve is peripheral, lacks website presence, and its option value has not materialized, making abandonment the better use of resources.
